chunks.text: In today's class, we will discuss the reading section of IELTS General Training.
Before we start discussing this lecture in detail, I want to remind you of one point.
In IELTS General Training, the reading and writing sections are different from the academic IELTS sections.
But the listening and speaking are very similar to the academic IELTS sections.
That's why we will follow the lessons of the academic IELTS for listening and speaking.
And for the general training, we will follow the reading and writing sections separately.
So today our main topic is how the reading section of general training is.
What is the reading section format?
In the first reading section of IELTS general training, there are two or three small factual texts.
Factual text means imagination.
Factual text means a scientific journal or a report.
There are two or three small texts based on real-life facts.
One of them can be a composite.
Composite means that there will be six to eight small texts based on the same topic.
Suppose you have two to three short factual texts in section one.
One of the texts will contain some small texts related to the topic.
For example, hotel advertisement.
Suppose you have one text where many small hotel ads are given.
That will be one text in section one.
There will be more than one text in section one.
What are the topics relevant to?
In English-speaking countries, such as the UK or America,
The topics in English-speaking countries are based on the common occurrences in daily life.
In section one.
Then there is section two.
There are two small factual texts in section two.
There are two short factual texts.
Which are based on work-related topics.
For example, apply for a job.
Or apply for a job.
Company policy.
It can be based on a company policy.
Pay and conditions.
For example, how to get a job in an industry.
How are the working conditions?
It can be related to this.
Workplace facilities.
Staff development.
Training.
You can see all of them.
All are related to work.
So, the section where there are two short factual texts.
And both are related to work.
In section three, there is a big complex text.
Which is based on a general interest.
The texts are authentic texts.
Authentic texts are sometimes from the notice.
Sometimes from the advertisement.
Sometimes from the newspaper.
Sometimes from the journal.
Sometimes from the report.
Sometimes from the official document, boy, magazine, newspaper.
These places are not directly.
Hence, they are called authentic texts.
What kind of questions are there in IELTS general training reading section?
All kinds of questions are coming one by one.
What can we see here?
The first thing we can see is matching headings.
Matching headings are like the IELTS academy.
It will give you a lot of headings.
It will tell you which paragraph's heading to choose.
Multiple choice questions are the same.
You have to give a question.
There will be some options.
You have to select one or two options from the options.
Identifying information.
It means that you will be given some information in the question.
It will tell you to find out where this information is in the passage.
Or identify it.
Matching information.
Matching information will give you some information.
And you have to match it.
You have to check where a similar fact has been said.
There will be a list.
You have to match the two lists.
Matching features.
This is also a technique to solve a problem.
Like matching information and identifying information.
Sentence completion.
We have studied sentence completion before.
There will be a gap in the end of a sentence.
You have to fill that gap by looking at the passage.
Summary.
We have to give a gap summary.
A summary that has many blanks.
We have to fill those blanks.
Table or flow chart completion.
A table or a flow chart of a process is given here.
You have to complete it by looking at the information on the passage.
True false and not given.
True false not given and IELTS academic are very similar.
You have to give a statement in the question.
Will say that it is true or false or not given in the passage.
If it is given in the same passage, then you select true.
If it is given in the opposite of the passage, then you select false.
If there is nothing in the passage, then you select not given.
And there are short answer questions.
Where you will be given a word limit of a word.
You have to give your answers according to that word limit.
We will discuss each individual question type in the next class.
Today we will discuss the format in this class.
In the reading section of IELTS general training.
Matching sentence ending is also a type of question.
You will be given many sentences and many endings.
You have to match which ending can be the ending of which sentence.
You have to decide this after reading the passage.
We have a sample answer sheet of the paper based exam in the general training reading section.
You can see here that your full name is written in capital letters.
So you write your name in block letters in this way.
My writing is a little off here.
But your writing should be clear here.
Write in block letters in a big hand.
Write your candidate number here.
Write 01234 as your candidate number.
Write your 3 digit language code in the box.
And shade the number in the grid on the right.
Write your language code here.
Write 012 as your language code.
Write 012 as your language code.
Mark the female and male.
Write the answer in the general training.
Write the answer in the option box.
Write the answer in the table if the answer is number 1.
Write the answer in the pencil if the answer is number 2.
Write in block letters so that you can understand the writing in your hand.
The examiner also says that the answers are written in block letters.
Because the answers are clearly understood by writing in block letters.
You must write the reading section with a pencil.
It is not advisable to write with a pen.
Keep an HB pencil with you and write the reading section with an HB pencil.
Write the answer of the reading section with an HB pencil.
If you look at the question pattern, mark and time,
The answer is the same in both cases.
If you take a computer-based IELTS exam,
You can write the reading section of the general training.
If you look at the question pattern,
The answer is written in block letters.
Mark the answer in the table.
If the answer is true, select true.
If the answer is 2, select 2.
Similarly, if you select 3, 4, 5, 6, the options will be displayed.
Write the answer in the blank.
Click on the black arrow in the corner.
You can go to the next page and answer the questions.
We will answer some common questions.
Is there any difference between the paper-based and computer-based IELTS exam?
The answer is the same in both cases.
The answer is the same in both cases.
The only difference is that the questions will be displayed on the computer screen.
You can easily win the exam by following the instructions given on the computer screen.
We have finished discussing the reading section of the general training.
In the next class, we will discuss each question in detail.
We will discuss all the questions in the reading section of the general training.

See you in the next class.
